protocol.codec_stress: Independently deliver original and source-time redraw of each paired LivePortrait and MuseTalk input as H.264 CRF 23 yuv420p. Preserve every rational source timestamp. Compare the same clips and exact edit ranges before and after final 4:2:0 delivery.
protocol.gate: At least four correctly localized strict LivePortrait redraws across three source groups, the strict MuseTalk edit, at least 70 percent measured coverage in each class, at most two ordinary flags and none on untouched, hard-cut or recompression controls. At least one half temporal IoU. Report the added codec stress separately.
protocol.input: Single decoded upright clip with verified native pictures and single-face geometry. No earlier copy, audio, supplied markers, or authoring metadata enters measurement.
protocol.measurement: At least 32 eligible pairs per parity per region, mean chroma step at least 0.6, and two supported reference patches. A shot needs at least 16 measured reference frames per used axis, median asymmetry magnitude at least 0.10, and 75 percent agreement in sign. Measure either the strongest admissible axis or both axes using their weaker loss.
protocol.phase: Measure horizontal and vertical adjacent-pixel color differences by native parity in the mouth ellipse and the two cheek and upper-face comparison patches. Exclude near-clipping and large luminance transitions, and cap chroma differences. Learn dominant axis and phase sign from the median surrounding patch response in each observed shot. A mouth score subtracts the signed mouth parity from the corresponding surrounding response.
protocol.point: Freeze the third-largest positive maximum among 56 ordinary GRID development clips, subject to a floor of 0.03, then require strict exceedance. Neither held bank is used for point selection.
protocol.range: Scan native 8, 12, 16, or 20 picture windows with five-picture flanks in one observed shot. Require at least 80 percent supported observations in the core and both flanks, and a positive median response relative to both flanks. Keep one strongest interval.
